forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.headline: Pay award inflation assumptions revised upward to 3% for 2027/28 and 2.5% for 2028/29, requiring additional £1.686m from MTFP over planning period
findings.detail: Following actual pay award of 3.3% for 2026/27 and wider trends in local government, budgeted pay award assumptions have been increased from 2.5% to 3% for 2027/28 and 2.5% for 2028/29. This incremental cost pressure of £1.686m over the period represents higher-than-expected workforce cost inflation.
findings.matters: Staffing typically represents the largest single cost item for local authorities. Higher-than-anticipated pay inflation is a structural pressure that compounds the budget challenge.
findings.figures: Revised assumptions: 3% for 2027/28, 2.5% for 2028/29, 2% from 2029/30; additional cost: £1.686m over 2027/28-2029/30
findings.quote: Given the recent years trend within local government and the wider inflationary outlook, the MTFP assumptions for the pay awards have been updated to 3% for 2027/28, 2.5% for 2028/29 and 2% for 2029/30 onwards. The updated assumption will require an additional £1.686m from the MTFP over the period 2027/28 to 2029/30

findings.headline: DSG cumulative deficit forecast at £38.316m by March 2027; government support committed to March 2028 but no clarity on treatment of deficits beyond that date, presenting significant future financial risk
findings.detail: The Dedicated Schools Grant deficit is forecast to reach £38.316m by March 2027, driven by High Needs Block demand growth. Government funds 90% of deficit up to March 2026 and has indicated support for deficits to March 2028 (subject to Local SEND Reform Plan approval). The Council remains responsible for 10%. No government detail has been provided on deficits arising beyond March 2028.
findings.matters: This represents a hidden future liability that could crystallize in 2028/29 when government support may end. The lack of clarity prevents robust medium-term planning.
findings.figures: £38.316m forecast deficit by March 2027; government funds 90% to March 2028; Council funds 10%
findings.quote: At this stage, no detail has been provided by Government regarding the treatment of deficits arising beyond March 2028 and this currently presents a significant financial risk in the future without Government intervention

findings.headline: Quarter One identified income shortfalls across commercial property, planning, building control, car parking and cultural services, raising questions about long-term achievability of income targets
findings.detail: Quarter One monitoring identified continuing income shortfalls across multiple fee-generating services. Whilst some are expected to improve, the paper identifies that several reflect wider changes in market conditions, occupancy levels and customer behaviour, suggesting structural rather than temporary income problems.
findings.matters: Income volatility across multiple services indicates systemic issues with income forecasting and reduces the reliability of budget planning. This compounds the challenge of closing the gap through sustainable solutions.
findings.figures: No aggregate figure provided; shortfalls identified across multiple service areas
findings.quote: Quarter One budget monitoring has identified continuing income shortfalls across commercial property, planning, building control, car parking, cultural services and other fee-generating activities. Whilst some of these pressures are expected to improve over time, several reflect wider changes in market conditions, occupancy levels and customer behaviour. This highlights the long-term achievability of some existing income targets

findings.headline: Unrestricted reserves would fall to negative balance by 2029/30 if provisional budget gap is not closed by permanent recurring measures, triggering Section 114 notice
findings.detail: The Council held £25.530m unrestricted reserves at 31 March 2026. If the forecast budget gaps are covered by reserves rather than solved through permanent measures, the usable unrestricted balance would deplete to (£0.2m) negative by 2029/30. The S151 Officer explicitly states this would force a Section 114 notice and application for Exceptional Financial Support from the Government.
findings.matters: This is the critical constraint. It quantifies precisely how much time the Council has to close the gap before formal financial distress. Section 114 notices signal effective insolvency and restrict authority operations.
findings.figures: Reserves at 31 March 2026: £25.530m; forecast negative balance: (£0.2m) by 2029/30
findings.quote: If the current forecast provisional budget gap for each year of the MTFP shown in Table 2 is not solved by permanent recurring measures then the level of Usable, Unrestricted Reserves would fall from £25.5m at the end of 2025/26, to a negative balance of (£0.2m) in 2029/30, i.e. all usable unrestricted reserves would be exhausted by 2029/30 and in that case the s151 Officer would be forced to issue a S114 notice

findings.headline: £2.845m of previously planned savings identified as unachievable or delayed, following £2.458m removed in February 2026
findings.detail: The Quarter One position has identified a further £2.845m of savings that are either unachievable or delayed (Children's Social Care, Environment, Communities & Culture, Regeneration & Housing and Council-wide budgets), added to £2.458m already removed in February 2026. The paper notes that removal of savings does not automatically trigger additional funding; services are still expected to find offsetting efficiencies elsewhere.
findings.matters: Savings plan collapse of this scale undermines the core budget strategy and means the Council must find even larger recurring solutions to close the gap.
findings.figures: £2.845m newly identified as unachievable or delayed; £2.458m previously removed in February 2026
findings.quote: the Quarter One 2026/27 financial monitoring position has identified a further £2.845m of savings that are either now considered unachievable or where delivery is expected to be delayed

daily_post.headline: £1.5m ICT Transformational programme deferred with no clear explanation of revised timescale
daily_post.lead: A major strategic capital programme being reprofiled without clear justification raises questions about strategic planning certainty and the council's ability to execute digital transformation, which affects longer-term operational efficiency.
